name: The Dave Hunt Rhythm and Blues band

podcast.title: Lull Coxhill's Early Role
podcast.body: The group featured soprano saxophone player Lull Coxhill, who was described as an "extremely good musician." Coxhill would later become "one of the most respected sax players in Britain" and a significant figure in the 1970s Canterbury scene, highlighting the band's strong musical talent. "their soprano saxophone player, Lull Coxill, would later become one of the most respected sax players in Britain, and was a big part of the canterbury scene in the 70s."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Ray Davis's Temporary Project
podcast.body: Ray Davis joined this group after an audition arranged by Giorgio Gomelsky. While with them, Ray played "Trad along with the blues," and it offered him "more prestigious gigs," temporarily making it seem like his original quartet was "over." Their repertoire included blues standards like "Honky Tonk Train Blues," played in the style of Bob Crosby's Bobcats. "Ray would later recall that the Dave Hunt band's repertoire included things like the old Mead Looks Lois Boogey piece, Honky Tonk Train Blues, which they would play in the style of Bob Crosby's Bobcats."
